subtopic: The Modulus and the Conjugate of a Complex Number
title: Worked (JEE Advanced): conjugate identities & product moduli

board_content.text: Advanced: z^2 = (z-bar)^2, and a big product
If $z^{2}=(\bar z)^{2}$, show $z$ is purely real or purely imaginary.
So $5\cdot 8\cdot 13\cdots(4+n^{2})=x^{2}+y^{2}$ — moduli tamed a scary product.

segments_english.text: <excited>Two Advanced-tier problems where the conjugate and modulus do all the heavy lifting.</excited>
First: if z squared equals z bar squared, prove that z must be purely real or purely imaginary.
Write z as x plus i y. Then z squared is x squared minus y squared, plus two i x y. And z bar squared is x squared minus y squared, minus two i x y.
Equating the two forces two x y to equal minus two x y, so four x y is zero, meaning the product x y is zero. That means either x is zero, purely imaginary, or y is zero, purely real. Done.
Second: the product of two plus i, two plus two i, up to two plus n i, equals some x plus i y. We want the value of five times eight times thirteen, and so on, up to four plus n squared.

Take the modulus across the product. The modulus of two plus k i is the root of four plus k squared, so the product of those roots equals the modulus of x plus i y, which is the root of x squared plus y squared.
Now square both sides: the product of four plus k squared, from k equals one to n, equals x squared plus y squared.
And that left side is exactly five times eight times thirteen and onward to four plus n squared. So the whole scary product equals x squared plus y squared. Modulus turned it into one clean line.

segments_hinglish.text: <excited>Do Advanced-tier problems jahan conjugate aur modulus saara heavy lifting karte hain.</excited>
Pehla: agar z square barabar z bar square, prove karo ki z purely real ya purely imaginary hona chahiye.
z ko x plus i y likho. To z square hai x square minus y square, plus two i x y. Aur z bar square hai x square minus y square, minus two i x y.
Dono ko equate karna two x y ko minus two x y ke barabar karta hai, to four x y zero, matlab product x y zero. Iska matlab ya to x zero, purely imaginary, ya y zero, purely real. Ho gaya.
Doosra: two plus i, two plus two i, up to two plus n i ka product, barabar koi x plus i y. Humein chahiye five times eight times thirteen, waise hi aage, up to four plus n square ki value.
Product par modulus lo. Two plus k i ka modulus hai four plus k square ka root, to un roots ka product barabar x plus i y ke modulus, jo hai x square plus y square ka root.
Ab dono taraf square karo: four plus k square ka product, k barabar one se n tak, barabar x square plus y square.
Aur wo left side bilkul wahi hai, five times eight times thirteen aur aage four plus n square tak. To poora scary product barabar x square plus y square. Modulus ne ise ek clean line bana diya.
